meta.case_name: Market Growth Strategy in Retail Banking

prompt.context: A bank based in a developing country in Southeast Asia has hired us to determine how it can grow in the local market, specifically in retail banking.
prompt.question: What are the factors you would look at to assess the situation? What is your recommendation for our client?

clarifying_info.q: What is the client's current market share and competitive position?
clarifying_info.a: Client is one of the top three market share leaders. Show Exhibit 1 and Exhibit 2.

clarifying_info.q: How are the client's products priced relative to competitors?
clarifying_info.a: All products are priced competitively at market level.

clarifying_info.q: What is the client's brand recognition?
clarifying_info.a: Client has good brand name reputation and recognition.

clarifying_info.q: What is the client's distribution network like?
clarifying_info.a: Client has wide distribution of branch and ATM network.

clarifying_info.q: What are the macroeconomic trends in this market?
clarifying_info.a: Number of people coming into employment age is at an all-time high in the coming 5 years. Foreign investments are projected for healthy growth with increased investments in Business Process Outsourcing. Interest rates have declined dramatically in the last 5 years from over 10% to the current level of 4%. Home/car ownership and real estate development is expected to increase in the coming 5 years. Rural to urban migration rate is stable.

clarifying_info.q: What is the income distribution of the population?
clarifying_info.a: 40% of the population lives at or below the poverty line. Another 40% makes less than $500 per month. Top 15% makes less than $2,000 per month. The remaining top 5% is the richest population whose lifestyle resembles upper-middle class in developed countries. Disposable income and GDP is projected to continue growing at about 11% per annum.

clarifying_info.q: What products does the bank offer?
clarifying_info.a: Products include savings, checking, time deposit, credit cards, and loans.
Most profitable products are credit cards and loans.

clarifying_info.q: What is the current product penetration in the population?
clarifying_info.a: 30% of the population has deposit accounts. 6% of the population has credit cards. 1.5% of the population has bank loans.

clarifying_info.q: What are the client's sales and marketing capabilities?
clarifying_info.a: Sales efforts are traditional and conservative. Client does not conduct direct marketing activities to sell credit cards. Sales force is stretched and training is lacking.

clarifying_info.q: What is the state of the client's IT and customer data?
clarifying_info.a: Information on customers is often out-dated.

clarifying_info.q: What is the client's R&D capability?
clarifying_info.a: R&D is competitive and client is a market leader in product innovation for a few products.

clarifying_info.q: What does the customer mix look like?
clarifying_info.a: Refer to Exhibit 3. Majority of customers only purchase one bank product. Large majority of customers also have less than 100K in average daily balance in their deposit accounts.

clarifying_info.q: What is the client's customer retention/attrition rate?
clarifying_info.a: Attrition rate is in line with the market average.

exhibits.title: Market Share and CAGR by Product
exhibits.shows: A table comparing market share (%) and 2002-2006 CAGR (%) for Deposits and Credit Cards across the Client, Competitor A, Competitor B, and Other banks, plus a Total Market row.

exhibits.title: Revenue/Volume by Product ($ Millions)
exhibits.shows: A table or chart showing financial figures (in millions of local currency) across the client's product lines, enabling comparison of size and growth across products.

exhibits.title: Customer Mix by Number of Products and Average Daily Balance
exhibits.shows: A chart or table showing the distribution of customers by how many bank products they hold and by the average daily balance in their deposit accounts.

data.observation: Majority of customers hold only one bank product; large majority have less than 100K in average daily balance.

framework: Competitive landscape: market share by bank and product, pricing, brand, distribution
Macroeconomic trends: employment/population growth, foreign investment, interest rate trends, GDP/disposable income growth, home/car ownership, urbanization
Products: product mix, profitability by product, product penetration rates in population
Client capabilities: sales and marketing effectiveness, IT/customer data quality, R&D and innovation
Customers: product holdings per customer, customer value (average daily balance), retention/attrition
Growth drivers: (1) steal share from competitors, (2) increase retention, (3) cross-sell to current customers, (4) up-sell to current customers, (5) develop new generation of customers

questions.prompt: Analyze Exhibit 1. What does the market share data tell you about the client's competitive position in Deposits vs. Credit Cards?
questions.guidance: Client maintained 15% market share in Deposits with CAGR of 10.6% (above total market 10.4%) — stable position. In Credit Cards, client's share dropped from a higher base to 10% with only 2.4% CAGR vs. the market's 7.5% CAGR, meaning client is losing credit card share rapidly. Competitor B is the strongest credit card grower (10.2% CAGR, 28% share). This signals a problem in credit cards specifically.

questions.prompt: Given the product penetration rates and profitability data, which growth lever should the client prioritize and why?
questions.guidance: Credit cards and loans are the most profitable products. Credit card penetration is only 6% and loan penetration only 1.5% — very low vs. the 30% with deposit accounts. The client has a large existing deposit customer base who do not yet hold more profitable products. Cross-selling credit cards and loans to existing deposit customers is the highest-ROI lever because acquisition cost is lower, data exists on these customers, and macro trends (rising incomes, falling interest rates, housing growth) support demand.

questions.prompt: Given macro trends (employment growth, 11% GDP growth, BPO investment), what new customer acquisition strategy would you recommend?
questions.guidance: A new generation of customers is entering employment age at an all-time high. The client should partner with employers to offer payroll accounts, thereby capturing new-to-bank customers at the point of first income. Separately, the client should partner with real estate developers and car dealers to provide home loans and auto loans at point of purchase, capturing customers with high loan intent.

brainstorming.prompt: What are all the possible growth drivers the client could pursue?

categories.name: Steal share from competitors
ideas: Aggressive credit card acquisition campaigns targeting competitor customers
Offer promotional interest rates or cash-back to switch deposit accounts
Leverage wider branch/ATM network as a competitive differentiator

categories.name: Increase retention of current customers
ideas: Improve customer data quality to enable proactive outreach
Train sales force on retention techniques

categories.name: Cross-sell products to current customers
ideas: Direct marketing of credit cards to existing deposit account holders
Targeted loan offers to customers with strong deposit track records
Bundle products (e.g., checking + credit card + home loan package)

categories.name: Up-sell current products
ideas: Move savings customers to higher-balance time deposit accounts
Upgrade credit card tiers for high-spend customers

categories.name: Develop new generation of customers
ideas: Partner with employers in BPO sector to capture young first-time earners via payroll banking
Partner with real estate developers to offer mortgage products to first-time home buyers
Partner with car dealers to provide auto loan financing at point of sale
Market basic savings accounts to the large population segment currently unbanked

recommendation: Prioritize cross-selling more profitable products (credit cards and loans) to existing deposit customers, since the average customer holds very few products and low-cost cross-sell channels already exist
Launch an aggressive, direct marketing campaign for credit cards targeting the existing deposit base to reverse the client's deteriorating credit card market share

Partner with employers (especially BPO sector), real estate developers, and car dealerships to capture the growing new generation of customers fueled by rising employment, income, and home/car ownership trends
risks: Credit quality risk if credit cards and loans are extended too broadly to customers with limited credit history in a developing market
Outdated customer IT data may reduce targeting effectiveness; requires IT investment before campaigns can be executed
Sales force capacity is currently stretched — scaling marketing aggressively without first improving training and headcount could damage service quality
next_steps: Upgrade customer information systems to ensure data is current and actionable for targeted marketing
Train and expand the sales force with a focus on credit card and loan products
Develop co-marketing partnerships with 2-3 major BPO employers and real estate developers as pilot programs
Track credit card market share quarterly to measure recovery against Competitor B
